subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: What boundary should OpenClaw enforce for protected config writes that originate from agent-visible errors, host exec, plugin cron work, or automated repair flows?
rationale: The remaining fix crosses persisted config, sandbox security posture, host exec authority, and plugin cron behavior; automation cannot safely choose whether to block CLI-through-exec writes, strip all assistant-visible config assignments, or allow some operator-copy guidance without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Enforce operator-approved protected writes
options.body: Remove protected config assignments from assistant-visible errors and require explicit operator provenance or approval for cron/plugin/exec paths that mutate sandbox or exec settings.

options.title: Land text hardening only
options.body: Treat actionable sandbox error wording as the immediate bug and keep a separate security follow-up for CLI-through-exec and plugin cron mutation boundaries.

options.title: Accept current operator-copy guidance
options.body: Keep the current hints and CLI patch behavior, accepting that host-exec-capable agents may be able to act on visible config advice in trusted deployments.

recommendation.title: Enforce operator-approved protected writes
recommendation.body: Remove protected config assignments from assistant-visible errors and require explicit operator provenance or approval for cron/plugin/exec paths that mutate sandbox or exec settings.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox/tool-policy and gateway-tool history makes this the best available routing owner for the security-boundary decision, with memory-core owners needed for the cron side.
